requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: Node1's dnsmasq is enabled and running, listens on 10.100.126.10:53 over TCP and UDP, and returns node2's address 10.100.126.11. The service and record remained functional after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: Node2 has nameserver 10.100.126.10 configured, resolves inventory-api.internal to its own address 10.100.126.11 through node1, and successfully reaches that hostname. These settings and behavior persisted across node2's restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct final behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered task-relevant service/configuration and DNS behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: Lifecycle failed-service collection used systemctl and was unsupported on Alpine, so it did not independently inventory failed OpenRC services.

The retained /etc/resolv.conf.head contents were not displayed after restart; its redundancy is inferred from the simultaneously retained 'nohook resolv.conf' configuration and manually managed /etc/resolv.conf.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related installation, configuration, service enablement, validation, and mandatory node restarts were appropriately scoped. Three minor unnecessary retained mutations were observed: cmd-5009a372337c44ad wrote /etc/resolv.conf.head even though the retained 'nohook resolv.conf' setting makes that file unnecessary for the chosen persistence design; cmd-0c51811dbbde409e and cmd-f44fd5d70b484881 each left /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log behind after the required restart protocol. The lifecycle snapshots confirm both temporary files remained. No damaged package state, broad exposure, or conflicting service was shown; dnsmasq is limited to node1's managed address.
